paragraphs: R. Chanina bar Pappi. Rav Yosef said, etc.; Abaye said to him, etc. They sent it before R. Chanina bar Pappi, who sent back a ruling like Rav Yosef's. Abaye said, “Did R. Chanina bar Pappi hang jewels on it?” They sent it before Rav Minyomi bar Rav Nechumi, etc. He told them, “Thus R. Yosef bar Minyomi said: R. Nachman said”—Ketubot 81b. A matron solicited R. Chanina bar Pappi. He said a word and filled himself with boils and sores; she said a word, and he healed. He fled and hid in a bathhouse where even two people entering by day would be harmed, because harmful spirits were found there. The rabbis asked, “Who guarded you?” He replied, “Two of Caesar's attendants”: Kiddushin 39b. There, 81a: Rav told Rav Yehudah, “Among upright men such as Rav Chanina bar Pappi and his colleagues.” Rashi explains: R. Tzadok and Rav Kahana. He did not go out to meet Rav Huna's coffin; see there. Gilgulei Neshamot [ג״נ] writes: R. Chanina bar Pappa—our reading is bar Pappi—was solicited by a matron, etc. She was Potiphera's wife, and R. Chanina bar Pappi was Menasheh son of Joseph. She came to tempt the son as she had tempted the father. Thus he fled, corresponding to “He fled outside,” to a dangerous place and was saved. A matron solicited R. Tzadok, etc.; see there. She returned to tempt R. Tzadok, who was Ephraim son of Joseph, but he did not heed her. She was then repaired: she had tried this three times, establishing a repeated pattern, and considered repentance. She told R. Tzadok, “Had I known it was so serious, I would not have distressed you.” End of quotation. Yuchasin regards this R. Tzadok as R. Elazar's father. The wording implies that she returned to tempt R. Tzadok after R. Chanina bar Pappi, tried three times, and repented inwardly when she told R. Tzadok, “Had I known ...” It appears that this R. Tzadok was not R. Elazar's father, who lived before the destruction. This also appears from the Gemara, which first brings R. Chanina bar Pappi's story and then R. Tzadok's. It requires investigation. R. Abba; R. Abbahu; R. Ilai; R. Zeira; R. Yochanan ben Elyakim; R. Yitzchak Nappacha; R. Elazar ben Pedat; R. Shimon ben Elyakim: see there. Rav Adda bar Avimi before him. And R. Yochanan; Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef; R. Ammi and R. Yitzchak Nappacha—Yevamot 68b. And R. Shimon ben Pazi.
